{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports a quantitative comparison of animal model results (QTc changes in NHP and canines at various drug concentrations) with human clinical outcomes (QTc changes at specific drug concentrations in humans), providing a measure of predictive accuracy for cardiovascular safety pharmacology.",
  "arm": "safety-pharmacology",
  "arm_evidence": "In preclinical cardiovascular safety pharmacology studies, statistical analysis of the rate corrected QT interval (QTc) is the focus for predicting QTc interval changes in the clinic.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cardiovascular"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "In preclinical cardiovascular safety pharmacology studies, statistical analysis of the rate corrected QT interval (QTc) is the focus for predicting QTc interval changes in the clinic.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "Cardiovascular telemetry studies were conducted in non-human primates (NHP; n = 48) and canines (n = 8).",
  "species": [
    "non-human-primate",
    "dog"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "Cardiovascular telemetry studies were conducted in non-human primates (NHP; n = 48) and canines (n = 8).",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "In NHP, a 10.9 ± 0.06 ms (mean ± 95% CI) change in QTc was detected at approximately 1.5× the moxifloxacin plasma concentration that causes a 10 ms QTc change in humans."
}
